nodes.name: App doors: manifest, install, tRPC, cron
nodes.summary: The routes Saleor, the dashboard iframe and the Vercel scheduler call that are not payment webhooks: manifest, register, tRPC (TypeScript remote procedure call) and the cleanup cron.
nodes.detail: Each route is a Next.js App Router handler wrapped with compose(withLoggerContext, withSpanAttributesAppRouter), so every request gets a logging context and OpenTelemetry span attributes. The manifest route tells Saleor which permissions and webhooks the app needs; Saleor then posts the app token to the register route, which stores it in the APL (Auth Persistence Layer, Amazon DynamoDB in production). The tRPC route serves the configuration screens and the cron route removes data of Saleor Cloud environments that no longer exist.

nodes.name: Saleor payment webhook handlers
nodes.summary: Seven webhook routes Saleor calls: six synchronous transaction events answered with a payment result, and the asynchronous ORDER_CREATED event.
nodes.detail: Every route is built from a SaleorSyncWebhook or SaleorAsyncWebhook definition (app SDK) that verifies Saleor's JSON Web Signature against its JSON Web Key Set, then withRecipientVerification rejects payloads addressed to another app ID with HTTP 403. The route validates the Saleor API address and schema version, then calls a use case class. Use cases return neverthrow Result values: an ok holds a typed response (success or a payment failure Saleor should record), an err holds an HTTP error response (400 App is not configured, 500 App is not working). Unexpected exceptions go to Sentry and answer 500 Unhandled error.

nodes.name: Shared webhook response plumbing
nodes.summary: Base response classes, recipient check and signature verification shared by every Saleor webhook route.
nodes.detail: SaleorSyncWebhook definitions call verifyWebhookSignature (JWKS, JSON Web Key Set, check) on the raw body; withRecipientVerification then compares payload.recipient.id with the app ID from the APL (Auth Persistence Layer) and answers 403 on mismatch. Response classes decide the HTTP status: payment outcomes are 200 with a result in the body, configuration or storage problems are 400 or 500.

nodes.name: PAYMENT_GATEWAY_INITIALIZE_SESSION
nodes.summary: Hands the storefront the Stripe publishable key configured for the checkout's channel.
nodes.detail: Synchronous event sent when the storefront calls paymentGatewayInitialize. The use case only reads DynamoDB; it never calls Stripe. The answer is { data: { stripePublishableKey } }.

nodes.name: TRANSACTION_INITIALIZE_SESSION
nodes.summary: Creates a Stripe PaymentIntent for a checkout or order and returns its client secret to the storefront.
nodes.detail: Synchronous event sent for transactionInitialize. This is where money starts moving: the app calls Stripe's PaymentIntents API, writes a RecordedTransaction to DynamoDB and returns the client secret in data.paymentIntent.stripeClientSecret. Unsupported payment methods and Stripe errors are answered as failure results so Saleor can show them; storage or mapping errors are HTTP 500 after the orphaned PaymentIntent is canceled.

nodes.name: TRANSACTION_PROCESS_SESSION
nodes.summary: Re-reads the PaymentIntent after the storefront confirmed it and returns its current Saleor result.
nodes.detail: Synchronous event sent for transactionProcess after Stripe.js confirmation or a redirect. The answer carries result, amount, pspReference, time, a dashboard link and payment method details so Saleor sees the current state before the Stripe event arrives.

nodes.name: TRANSACTION_CHARGE_REQUESTED
nodes.summary: Captures an authorized PaymentIntent when staff or Saleor ask to charge it.
nodes.detail: Synchronous event sent when an AUTHORIZATION_SUCCESS transaction is charged from the dashboard or by Saleor. The app captures the full PaymentIntent with Saleor's idempotency key and answers CHARGE_SUCCESS with the captured amount.

nodes.name: TRANSACTION_REFUND_REQUESTED
nodes.summary: Creates a Stripe refund and answers asynchronously; the final refund status arrives through the Stripe webhook.
nodes.detail: Synchronous event sent when staff request a refund. The app creates the refund in Stripe and answers only its ID; Stripe's charge.refund.updated event later reports REFUND_SUCCESS or REFUND_FAILURE through transactionEventReport.

nodes.name: TRANSACTION_CANCELATION_REQUESTED
nodes.summary: Cancels a not yet captured PaymentIntent.
nodes.detail: Synchronous event sent when staff void an authorization. The app cancels the PaymentIntent with Saleor's idempotency key and answers CANCEL_SUCCESS with the canceled_at time, or CANCEL_FAILURE.

nodes.name: ORDER_CREATED (order data sync)
nodes.summary: Writes the new order's ID and number onto the PaymentIntents this app created during checkout.
nodes.detail: Asynchronous event (Saleor retries non-2xx answers). It only adds metadata and a description to PaymentIntents; payment state is never changed here.

nodes.name: Stripe event receiver
nodes.summary: The single route Stripe calls with payment_intent.* and charge.refund.updated events, which the app turns into Saleor transaction events.
nodes.detail: Stripe posts to /api/webhooks/stripe with saleorApiUrl, configurationId and appId query parameters the app put into the endpoint address when it created it. The use case loads the installation from the APL (Auth Persistence Layer), detects webhooks left over from an earlier installation and deletes them, loads the configuration, verifies the Stripe-Signature header with the stored signing secret, dispatches to a PaymentIntent or Refund handler and reports the mapped result with the transactionEventReport GraphQL mutation. Events for objects not created by this installation are acknowledged with 200 so Stripe stops retrying.

nodes.name: Stripe API layer
nodes.summary: Thin wrappers around the Stripe Node SDK: client setup, PaymentIntents, refunds, webhook endpoints, signature checks, money conversion and the branded value types.
nodes.detail: Every call creates a Stripe client from the configuration's restricted key, pinned to API version 2025-04-30.basil, using the fetch HTTP client so tests can mock it. Calls are wrapped in neverthrow ResultAsync so use cases never see exceptions; Stripe errors are mapped to app error classes with a public code, a storefront message and a merchant message. Keys, IDs and statuses are Zod branded types (ADR, architecture decision record, 0002).

nodes.name: Transaction results and status mapping
nodes.summary: Classes for every Saleor transaction result the app can answer (CHARGE_SUCCESS, AUTHORIZATION_ACTION_REQUIRED, REFUND_FAILURE...) and the functions that map Stripe statuses onto them.
nodes.detail: Each result class carries the Saleor result enum value, the actions staff may take next (CHARGE, CANCEL, REFUND) and a human message. Webhook responses and transactionEventReport calls read these three fields, so the mapping from Stripe PaymentIntent and Refund statuses lives in one place.

nodes.name: Saleor-side domain and event reporting
nodes.summary: Saleor value types (API address, money, transaction ID and flow), helpers that read requested-event payloads, the channel fetcher and the transactionEventReport client.
nodes.detail: Value types are Zod branded types so a Saleor API address cannot be passed where an app ID is expected. Requested-event helpers throw when the payload has no transaction or channel, which older subscription queries could produce. TransactionEventReporter is the only place the app writes payment state back to Saleor.

nodes.name: Stripe configuration store and screens
nodes.summary: Per-installation Stripe configurations (publishable key, encrypted restricted key and webhook secret), their channel mapping in DynamoDB, and the tRPC procedures behind the settings screens.
nodes.detail: A configuration holds a name, a publishable key, a restricted key and the ID and signing secret of the Stripe webhook endpoint the app created for it. Channels map to at most one configuration. Both live in one Amazon DynamoDB table under the partition key '<saleorApiUrl>#<appId>', so a reinstall starts empty. The restricted key and the webhook secret are encrypted with AES-256-CBC (Advanced Encryption Standard) using SECRET_KEY, with fallback keys accepted for decryption during key rotation. The tRPC procedures validate the dashboard user's JSON Web Token before reading or writing.

nodes.name: Configuration domain and DynamoDB repo
nodes.summary: The StripeConfig and AppRootConfig models, the AppConfigRepo interface and its DynamoDB implementation.
nodes.detail: The repo interface hides storage so a fork can swap DynamoDB (app-config-repo-impl.ts is the single switch). StripeConfig.create enforces that the publishable and restricted keys are both test or both live keys. Configurations are loaded either by channel (Saleor webhooks) or by configuration ID (Stripe webhooks, whose address carries it).

nodes.name: tRPC configuration procedures
nodes.summary: Procedures the settings pages call: list, create, update and remove configurations, list channels and change the channel mapping.
nodes.detail: All procedures use protectedClientProcedure, so they require a valid dashboard JSON Web Token (JWT) with MANAGE_APPS and HANDLE_PAYMENTS. Creating, rotating or removing a configuration also creates, recreates or deletes its Stripe webhook endpoint; App Problems for the configuration are cleared after an update or removal.

nodes.name: Transaction recording
nodes.summary: Remembers, per PaymentIntent, which Saleor transaction it belongs to and whether it runs as charge or authorization, so later events can be mapped.
nodes.detail: TRANSACTION_INITIALIZE_SESSION writes one item per PaymentIntent (sort key TRANSACTION#<paymentIntentId>) with a condition that the item does not exist yet. TRANSACTION_PROCESS_SESSION and the Stripe event handlers read it back; a missing item is an error, not a null, because it means the business flow broke.

nodes.name: Runtime platform: env, logs, tracing, APL
nodes.summary: Environment validation, the APL (Auth Persistence Layer) that stores app tokens, request-scoped context, logging, tracing, Sentry setup, the DynamoDB client and App Problems reporting.
nodes.detail: Everything request-scoped uses AsyncLocalStorage: the logger context (attributes on every log line) and AppContext (TEST or LIVE Stripe mode). The DynamoDB main table holds both the APL and app data. Sentry and OpenTelemetry are loaded only when their environment variables are set.

nodes.name: Configuration user interface
nodes.summary: Next.js Pages Router screens rendered inside the Saleor Dashboard iframe: configuration list, create and edit forms, channel assignment and the order sync callout.
nodes.detail: Pages are wrapped in AppBridgeProvider and GraphQLProvider from the app SDK and call the tRPC procedures through trpcClient (React Query). Components come from @saleor/apps-ui-next, the dashboard-aligned kit described in ADR (architecture decision record) 0004.

nodes.name: Build, scripts and generated code
nodes.summary: Package scripts, Next.js and Vercel settings, GraphQL documents and generated types, and the deploy, migration, key rotation and local DynamoDB scripts.
nodes.detail: pnpm deploy runs next build and then the webhooks migration against every installation. Types are generated twice: GraphQL documents through graphql-codegen, and synchronous webhook response types from Saleor's published JSON schemas pinned by the package's saleor schemaVersion.

nodes.name: App manifest route
nodes.summary: Builds the app manifest: HANDLE_PAYMENTS and MANAGE_ORDERS permissions, Saleor 3.23 to below 4, and seven webhook subscriptions.
nodes.detail: manifestFactory reads APP_IFRAME_BASE_URL and APP_API_BASE_URL (falling back to the request's base address) so the iframe and the API can live on different hosts. tokenTargetUrl points Saleor at /api/register. The webhook list is produced by calling getWebhookManifest on each webhook definition, so subscription queries and target addresses come from one source. MANAGE_ORDERS was added for ORDER_CREATED; older installations grant it later from the app screen (order sync module).
nodes.code:
permissions: ["HANDLE_PAYMENTS", "MANAGE_ORDERS"],
      requiredSaleorVersion: ">=3.23 <4",
      supportUrl: "https://saleor.io/discord",
      tokenTargetUrl: `${apiBaseUrl}/api/register`,
      version: packageJson.version,
      webhooks: [
        paymentGatewayInitializeSessionWebhookDefinition.getWebhookManifest(apiBaseUrl),
        transactionInitializeSessionWebhookDefinition.getWebhookManifest(apiBaseUrl),
        transactionProcessSessionWebhookDefinition.getWebhookManifest(apiBaseUrl),
        transactionChargeRequestedWebhookDefinition.getWebhookManifest(apiBaseUrl),
        transactionCancelationRequestedWebhookDefinition.getWebhookManifest(apiBaseUrl),
        transactionRefundRequestedWebhookDefinition.getWebhookManifest(apiBaseUrl),
        orderCreatedWebhookDefinition.getWebhookManifest(apiBaseUrl),
      ],

nodes.name: GET /api/manifest
nodes.summary: Returns the app manifest JSON Saleor reads when the app is installed or updated.

nodes.name: App install (register) route
nodes.summary: Receives the app token Saleor posts during installation and saves it in the APL (Auth Persistence Layer), optionally restricted to Saleor addresses matching ALLOWED_DOMAIN_PATTERN.
nodes.detail: createAppRegisterHandler from the app SDK verifies the request and writes saleorApiUrl, appId and token to saleorApp.apl. When ALLOWED_DOMAIN_PATTERN is set it is compiled into a regular expression and installations from other Saleor hosts are refused and logged; unset, every host is allowed. Failures to save are logged through onAplSetFailed.
facts: ALLOWED_DOMAIN_PATTERN unset allows every Saleor instance

nodes.name: POST /api/register
nodes.summary: Token target address Saleor calls once per installation with the app's auth token.

nodes.name: tRPC route
nodes.summary: Serves the tRPC (TypeScript remote procedure call) router at /api/trpc with fetchRequestHandler; internal server errors are logged at error level, others at debug.
facts: Exports the same handler as GET and POST
nodes.detail: fetchRequestHandler builds the tRPC context from request headers (dashboard token, Saleor API address, Origin as app address) and dispatches to trpcRouter. It is wrapped like every route with the logger context and span attributes.

nodes.name: POST /api/trpc/{trpc}
nodes.summary: Entry for every configuration and order sync procedure the settings pages call.

nodes.name: Stale installations cleanup cron
nodes.summary: Daily Vercel cron, guarded by CRON_SECRET, that deletes data and Stripe webhooks of installations whose Saleor Cloud environment is gone.
nodes.detail: withCronAuthAppRouter answers 401 unless the Authorization header carries the bearer CRON_SECRET (constant-time compare, refuses everything while unset). cleanupStaleInstallations from the shared package asks Saleor Cloud which installations still exist; before deleting a tenant's DynamoDB items it calls createRemoveInstallationStripeWebhooks, which deletes each configuration's Stripe webhook endpoint with its restricted key. STALE_INSTALLATIONS_CLEANUP_DRY_RUN logs without deleting.
facts: Only runs the table cleanup when APL is dynamodb

nodes.name: GET /api/cron/cleanup-stale-installations
nodes.summary: Called by Vercel Cron with the CRON_SECRET bearer token.

nodes.name: Webhook response base classes
nodes.summary: SuccessWebhookResponse (HTTP 200) and the error responses BrokenApp (500), AppIsNotConfigured (400), UnhandledError (500) and MalformedRequest (500).
nodes.detail: Every use case response extends SuccessWebhookResponse even when it reports a payment failure, because Saleor reads the failure from the JSON body. Error responses are real HTTP errors. Messages pass through ResponseMessageFormatter, which appends the underlying error message only when the configuration is a Stripe TEST one, so live storefronts never see internals. The shared Zod helpers in saleor-webhook-response-schema.ts shape the data.paymentIntent field.

nodes.name: withRecipientVerification()
nodes.summary: Wrapper that answers HTTP 403 when the webhook payload's recipient ID differs from the app ID stored for that Saleor instance.

nodes.name: Saleor signature verifier
nodes.summary: Re-exports verifySignatureWithJwks from the app SDK; every synchronous webhook definition passes it as verifySignatureFn.

nodes.name: TRANSACTION_INITIALIZE_SESSION route
nodes.summary: Handles TRANSACTION_INITIALIZE_SESSION: records the amount in the log context, validates the Saleor address and schema version, then runs the use case.
nodes.detail: The webhook definition (webhook-definition.ts) names the event, the subscription query and the path; createHandler verifies the request, loads auth data from the APL (Auth Persistence Layer) and parses the payload. The handler sets observability attributes, rejects a malformed Saleor address, creates the App Problems reporter and calls the use case; ok and err results are both rendered with getResponse(). Thrown errors go to Sentry and answer 500.

nodes.name: POST .../saleor/transaction-initialize-session
nodes.summary: Target of the TRANSACTION_INITIALIZE_SESSION webhook declared in webhook-definition.ts.

nodes.name: TransactionInitializeSessionUseCase
nodes.summary: Creates a Stripe PaymentIntent for the transaction and answers CHARGE_ or AUTHORIZATION_ACTION_REQUIRED with the client secret.

nodes.name: TransactionInitializeSessionUseCase.execute()
nodes.summary: Creates a Stripe PaymentIntent for the transaction and answers CHARGE_ or AUTHORIZATION_ACTION_REQUIRED with the client secret.
nodes.detail: Parses event.data (the storefront's paymentIntent.paymentMethod) against the eleven supported payment method schemas; an unknown method answers a failure and reports an App Problem. Loads the Stripe configuration mapped to the checkout's channel (400 when none). Resolves the payment method object, which decides the real flow (for example SEPA Debit always charges) and the payment_method_options; card switches capture_method to manual for authorization. Builds the PaymentIntent with automatic_payment_methods enabled, metadata (saleor_transaction_id, saleor_api_url, saleor_app_id, source and order IDs) and Saleor's idempotency key, then calls Stripe. A Stripe error answers CHARGE_FAILURE or AUTHORIZATION_FAILURE with the mapped public code (and an App Problem for authentication or permission errors). On success it writes a RecordedTransaction to DynamoDB; if that write or the response mapping fails, it cancels the orphaned PaymentIntent before answering 500.

nodes.name: prepareStripeCreatePaymentIntentParams()
nodes.summary: Converts Saleor's amount to Stripe's smallest currency unit and assembles PaymentIntent metadata, description and payment method options.
nodes.detail: StripeMoney.createFromSaleorAmount rejects negative amounts and unknown currencies and rounds with the currency's digit count from currency-codes. The order number becomes the description 'Saleor Order #<number>' when the source object is an order. Metadata carries the IDs the Stripe webhook later needs to find the Saleor transaction and to reject objects from other installations.

nodes.name: Initialize-session data parser
nodes.summary: Zod discriminated union over paymentIntent.paymentMethod; distinguishes an unsupported method (UnsupportedPaymentMethodError) from malformed data (ParseError).
nodes.detail: The storefront passes data to the transactionInitializeSession mutation and Saleor forwards it as event.data. The schema is strict, so extra keys fail. Both errors carry a publicCode and publicMessage for the storefront and a merchantMessage for staff.

nodes.name: Payment method resolver
nodes.summary: Switch from the parsed paymentMethod string to the PaymentMethod class (card, klarna, google_pay, apple_pay, paypal, us_bank_account, sepa_debit, link, pay_by_bank, mobilepay, revolut_pay).

nodes.name: PAYMENT_GATEWAY_INITIALIZE_SESSION route
nodes.summary: Handles PAYMENT_GATEWAY_INITIALIZE_SESSION and returns the channel's publishable key to the storefront.
nodes.detail: The webhook definition (webhook-definition.ts) names the event, the subscription query and the path; createHandler verifies the request, loads auth data from the APL (Auth Persistence Layer) and parses the payload. The handler sets observability attributes, rejects a malformed Saleor address, creates the App Problems reporter and calls the use case; ok and err results are both rendered with getResponse(). Thrown errors go to Sentry and answer 500.

nodes.name: POST .../payment-gateway-initialize-session
nodes.summary: Target of the PAYMENT_GATEWAY_INITIALIZE_SESSION webhook declared in webhook-definition.ts.

nodes.name: PaymentGatewayInitializeSessionUseCase
nodes.summary: Looks up the configuration for the channel and answers data.stripePublishableKey.

nodes.name: PaymentGatewayInitializeSessionUseCase.execute()
nodes.summary: Looks up the configuration for the channel and answers data.stripePublishableKey.
nodes.detail: Calls AppConfigRepo.getStripeConfig by channel ID. A missing configuration answers 400 App is not configured, a storage error 500. On success it stores the Stripe environment (TEST or LIVE, from the publishable key prefix) in the request context and returns the publishable key, which Stripe.js on the storefront needs.

nodes.name: TRANSACTION_PROCESS_SESSION route
nodes.summary: Handles TRANSACTION_PROCESS_SESSION after the storefront confirmed the payment with Stripe.js.
nodes.detail: The webhook definition (webhook-definition.ts) names the event, the subscription query and the path; createHandler verifies the request, loads auth data from the APL (Auth Persistence Layer) and parses the payload. The handler sets observability attributes, rejects a malformed Saleor address, creates the App Problems reporter and calls the use case; ok and err results are both rendered with getResponse(). Thrown errors go to Sentry and answer 500.

nodes.name: POST .../saleor/transaction-process-session
nodes.summary: Target of the TRANSACTION_PROCESS_SESSION webhook declared in webhook-definition.ts.

nodes.name: TransactionProcessSessionUseCase
nodes.summary: Retrieves the PaymentIntent and the recorded transaction and answers the mapped Saleor result with amount, timestamp and card details.

nodes.name: TransactionProcessSessionUseCase.execute()
nodes.summary: Retrieves the PaymentIntent and the recorded transaction and answers the mapped Saleor result with amount, timestamp and card details.
nodes.detail: Loads the channel configuration, retrieves the PaymentIntent (expanding payment_method) and the RecordedTransaction from DynamoDB by the pspReference. The recorded resolved flow (CHARGE or AUTHORIZATION) plus the PaymentIntent status go through mapPaymentIntentStatusToTransactionResult. A Stripe error answers a failure result and, for authentication or permission errors, reports an App Problem. Payment method details (card brand, last digits, expiry) are attached when Stripe returns them.

nodes.name: TRANSACTION_CHARGE_REQUESTED route
nodes.summary: Handles TRANSACTION_CHARGE_REQUESTED, sent when an authorized payment should be captured.
nodes.detail: The webhook definition (webhook-definition.ts) names the event, the subscription query and the path; createHandler verifies the request, loads auth data from the APL (Auth Persistence Layer) and parses the payload. The handler sets observability attributes, rejects a malformed Saleor address, creates the App Problems reporter and calls the use case; ok and err results are both rendered with getResponse(). Thrown errors go to Sentry and answer 500.

nodes.name: POST .../saleor/transaction-charge-requested
nodes.summary: Target of the TRANSACTION_CHARGE_REQUESTED webhook declared in webhook-definition.ts.

nodes.name: TransactionChargeRequestedUseCase
nodes.summary: Captures the PaymentIntent named by pspReference and answers CHARGE_SUCCESS or CHARGE_FAILURE.

nodes.name: TransactionChargeRequestedUseCase.execute()
nodes.summary: Captures the PaymentIntent named by pspReference and answers CHARGE_SUCCESS or CHARGE_FAILURE.
nodes.detail: Reads the transaction, channel and idempotency key from the requested-event payload (order or checkout). Calls paymentIntents.capture with Saleor's idempotency key and the order metadata (order ID, number, checkout ID). A Stripe error answers CHARGE_FAILURE with a link to the Stripe dashboard and reports an App Problem when it is an authentication or permission error.

nodes.name: TRANSACTION_REFUND_REQUESTED route
nodes.summary: Handles TRANSACTION_REFUND_REQUESTED, sent when staff refund a payment.
nodes.detail: The webhook definition (webhook-definition.ts) names the event, the subscription query and the path; createHandler verifies the request, loads auth data from the APL (Auth Persistence Layer) and parses the payload. The handler sets observability attributes, rejects a malformed Saleor address, creates the App Problems reporter and calls the use case; ok and err results are both rendered with getResponse(). Thrown errors go to Sentry and answer 500.

nodes.name: POST .../saleor/transaction-refund-requested
nodes.summary: Target of the TRANSACTION_REFUND_REQUESTED webhook declared in webhook-definition.ts.

nodes.name: TransactionRefundRequestedUseCase
nodes.summary: Creates a Stripe refund for the requested amount and answers only its pspReference; the result arrives later via charge.refund.updated.

nodes.name: TransactionRefundRequestedUseCase.execute()
nodes.summary: Creates a Stripe refund for the requested amount and answers only its pspReference; the result arrives later via charge.refund.updated.
nodes.detail: Converts the requested amount with StripeMoney, then calls refunds.create on the PaymentIntent with Saleor's idempotency key and metadata (saleor_transaction_id, saleor_api_url, saleor_app_id, order IDs). Because Saleor does not accept REFUND_REQUEST as a synchronous answer, success returns the asynchronous shape { pspReference: refund ID }. A Stripe error answers REFUND_FAILURE with the merchant message and a dashboard link.

nodes.name: TRANSACTION_CANCELATION_REQUESTED route
nodes.summary: Handles TRANSACTION_CANCELATION_REQUESTED for authorized payments that should be released.
nodes.detail: The webhook definition (webhook-definition.ts) names the event, the subscription query and the path; createHandler verifies the request, loads auth data from the APL (Auth Persistence Layer) and parses the payload. The handler sets observability attributes, rejects a malformed Saleor address, creates the App Problems reporter and calls the use case; ok and err results are both rendered with getResponse(). Thrown errors go to Sentry and answer 500.

nodes.name: POST .../transaction-cancelation-requested
nodes.summary: Target of the TRANSACTION_CANCELATION_REQUESTED webhook declared in webhook-definition.ts.

nodes.name: TransactionCancelationRequestedUseCase
nodes.summary: Cancels the PaymentIntent and answers CANCEL_SUCCESS or CANCEL_FAILURE.

nodes.name: TransactionCancelationRequestedUseCase.execute()
nodes.summary: Cancels the PaymentIntent and answers CANCEL_SUCCESS or CANCEL_FAILURE.
nodes.detail: Uses the channel configuration's restricted key to call paymentIntents.cancel with Saleor's idempotency key. On success the answer carries the PaymentIntent amount and its timestamp; on a Stripe error it answers CANCEL_FAILURE and, for authentication or permission errors, reports an App Problem.

nodes.name: ORDER_CREATED route
nodes.summary: Handles the asynchronous ORDER_CREATED event; answers 500 on failure so Saleor retries, since the update is idempotent.
nodes.detail: The webhook definition (webhook-definition.ts) names the event, the subscription query and the path; createHandler verifies the request, loads auth data from the APL (Auth Persistence Layer) and parses the payload. The handler sets observability attributes, rejects a malformed Saleor address, creates the App Problems reporter and calls the use case; ok and err results are both rendered with getResponse(). Thrown errors go to Sentry and answer 500.

nodes.name: POST /api/webhooks/saleor/order-created
nodes.summary: Target of the ORDER_CREATED webhook declared in webhook-definition.ts.

nodes.name: OrderCreatedUseCase
nodes.summary: Copies the order ID, number and checkout ID onto this app's PaymentIntents once checkout became an order.

nodes.name: OrderCreatedUseCase.execute()
nodes.summary: Copies the order ID, number and checkout ID onto this app's PaymentIntents once checkout became an order.
nodes.detail: PaymentIntents created during checkout do not know the order yet. The use case keeps only the order's transactions created by this app (createdBy.id equals the app ID) whose pspReference starts with pi_, loads the channel configuration (skips quietly when none) and calls paymentIntents.update for each with the metadata and the description 'Saleor Order #<number>'. It stops at the first Stripe error. Requires MANAGE_ORDERS; older installations enable it from the order sync callout.

nodes.name: Stripe webhook route
nodes.summary: Parses the Stripe-Signature header and the saleorApiUrl, configurationId and appId query parameters, then runs StripeWebhookUseCase.
nodes.detail: Missing header or invalid parameters answer 400 Malformed request before any lookup. The use case is built once with its dependencies: the DynamoDB config repo, the APL (Auth Persistence Layer), the transaction recorder, a TransactionEventReporter factory that makes an instrumented GraphQL client from the installation's auth data, the App Problems reporter, StripeWebhookManager and the PaymentIntents API factory. Unexpected exceptions are wrapped, sent to Sentry and answered 500 so Stripe retries.
facts: 400 responses: malformed request, app not configured, transaction missing

nodes.name: POST /api/webhooks/stripe
nodes.summary: Endpoint registered in each merchant's Stripe account per configuration; receives payment_intent.* and charge.refund.updated events.

nodes.name: WebhookParams
nodes.summary: Parses the query parameters Stripe echoes back: saleorApiUrl (must end in /graphql/), configurationId (a UUID, universally unique identifier) and appId (at least 3 characters).
nodes.detail: The app ID is kept in the address so that, after a reinstall, the app can still find the old configuration (its DynamoDB key includes the app ID) and delete the leftover endpoint.

nodes.name: StripeWebhookUseCase
nodes.summary: Verifies a Stripe event against the configuration's signing secret, dispatches it by object type and reports the result to Saleor.

nodes.name: StripeWebhookUseCase.execute()
nodes.summary: Loads auth data and configuration, verifies the event, processes it and calls transactionEventReport; maps each failure to a 200, 400 or 500 answer.
nodes.detail: Steps: APL lookup by saleorApiUrl (missing answers 400). If the appId in the address differs from the installed app ID, the webhook belongs to an earlier installation: processLegacyWebhook deletes it and the event is acknowledged. Loads the configuration by configurationId (missing reports an App Problem and answers 400), sets the TEST or LIVE environment in context, verifies the signature with stripe.webhooks.constructEvent (failure reports a webhook secret mismatch problem). Objects without saleor_transaction_id metadata (created outside Saleor) and objects from another installation are acknowledged with 200. A missing recorded transaction answers 400; other processing errors 500. The resolved variables are reported with transactionEventReport; ALREADY_EXISTS or alreadyProcessed counts as success.
nodes.signature: async execute({ rawBody, signatureHeader, webhookParams }): R

nodes.name: StripeWebhookUseCase.processEvent()
nodes.summary: Switches on event.data.object.object: payment_intent goes to StripePaymentIntentHandler, refund to StripeRefundHandler, anything else throws.
nodes.detail: Before dispatching it checks the object's metadata: no saleor_transaction_id means ObjectMetadataMissingError; a saleor_app_id different from the current one means ObjectMetadataMismatchError. Objects created before saleor_app_id existed are accepted.

nodes.name: processLegacyWebhook()
nodes.summary: Deletes a Stripe endpoint left from an earlier installation, using the old configuration found with the app ID frozen in the webhook address.
nodes.detail: If the old configuration is already gone the app cannot authenticate to delete it, so it reports an App Problem asking staff to remove it in the Stripe Dashboard.

nodes.name: StripePaymentIntentHandler
nodes.summary: Turns six payment_intent events into TransactionEventReportVariablesResolver objects using the recorded transaction flow.

nodes.name: processPaymentIntentEvent()
nodes.summary: Reads the recorded transaction, converts the amount, fetches card details and maps the event: status mapping for four event types, failure or cancel results for the other two.
nodes.detail: payment_intent.payment_failed becomes AUTHORIZATION_FAILURE or CHARGE_FAILURE depending on the recorded flow; payment_intent.canceled becomes CANCEL_SUCCESS. The event time comes from event.created. Card details come from a separate paymentIntents.retrieve call and fall back to null on error, so a lookup failure never blocks the report.

nodes.name: StripeRefundHandler
nodes.summary: Handles charge.refund.updated: finds the PaymentIntent behind the refund, reads the recorded transaction and maps the refund status.
nodes.detail: Only charge.refund.updated is supported. The refund's payment_intent may be an ID or an expanded object; a refund without one is a MalformedEventError. The reported pspReference is the refund ID and the amount is the refund amount.

nodes.name: processRefundEvent()
nodes.summary: Builds the report variables for a refund event with mapRefundStatusToTransactionResult.

nodes.name: Event report variables resolver
nodes.summary: Value object holding transaction ID, amount, result, time, Stripe object ID, dashboard link and payment method details; resolveEventReportVariables() shapes them for the mutation.

nodes.name: StripeClient
nodes.summary: Single place where the Stripe SDK is constructed from a restricted key, pinned to API version 2025-04-30.basil and tagged with app info (name, version, APPSTORE_URL, STRIPE_PARTNER_ID).

nodes.name: StripePaymentIntentsApi
nodes.summary: create, retrieve (expanding payment_method), capture, cancel and update PaymentIntents, each wrapped in ResultAsync; created per request by StripePaymentIntentsApiFactory.

nodes.name: StripeRefundsApi
nodes.summary: Creates refunds on a PaymentIntent with amount, metadata and idempotency key; built per request by StripeRefundsApiFactory.

nodes.name: StripeWebhookManager
nodes.summary: Creates, reads, updates and deletes the Stripe webhook endpoint that belongs to each configuration.
nodes.detail: createWebhook builds the address /api/webhooks/stripe?configurationId=...&saleorApiUrl=...&appId=... (StripeWebhookUrlBuilder), subscribes to the supported events, pins the API version and stores the configuration ID in endpoint metadata; the signing secret is only returned on creation, so a missing one is treated as a panic. isWebhookReachableWithKey answers false only for resource_missing, so a transient Stripe error never causes a duplicate endpoint during key rotation.
facts: Events: payment_intent.amount_capturable_updated, payment_failed, processing, requires_action, succeeded, canceled
Description: Created by Saleor App Payment Stripe, config name: <name>

nodes.name: StripeWebhookManager.createWebhook()
nodes.summary: Registers the endpoint in the merchant's Stripe account and returns its ID and signing secret.

nodes.name: Stripe signature validator
nodes.summary: Wraps stripe.webhooks.constructEvent in fromThrowable, turning a bad signature or body into StripeEventParsingError.

nodes.name: Restricted key validator
nodes.summary: Checks a restricted key by listing one PaymentIntent; used before saving or changing keys.

nodes.name: Stripe error mapping
nodes.summary: Maps Stripe SDK errors (card, invalid request, rate limit, connection, API, authentication, permission, idempotency, unknown) to app errors with public and merchant messages.
nodes.detail: Card errors use Stripe's own message for the storefront, as Stripe recommends; every other kind gets the generic StripeApiError public code. Authentication and permission errors trigger App Problems for the configuration.

nodes.name: StripeMoney
nodes.summary: Converts a Saleor decimal amount to Stripe's integer minor units using the currency's digit count (currency.js and currency-codes) and lowercases the currency.
facts: Rejects amounts below 0, so 0 is allowed
Rejects currency codes that are not 3 letters or unknown

nodes.name: Installation webhook removal
nodes.summary: For the stale installations cron: deletes every configuration's Stripe endpoint; 401, 403 and 404 count as done, other errors keep the installation for the next run.
nodes.detail: Configurations encrypted with a key that is no longer configured cannot be read, so they are skipped rather than retried forever.

nodes.name: Order metadata for Stripe
nodes.summary: Builds saleor_order_id, saleor_order_number and saleor_checkout_id metadata and the 'Saleor Order #<number>' description.

nodes.name: Branded keys and secrets
nodes.summary: Zod branded types for the restricted key (rk_test_/rk_live_ expected), publishable key, webhook secret and client secret.
nodes.detail: Each key type is a Zod schema with .brand(). The restricted key schema accepts any non-empty value but sends a Sentry warning when it lacks the rk_test_ or rk_live_ prefix, so unexpected formats are seen without blocking merchants.

nodes.name: Branded IDs, statuses and timestamps
nodes.summary: Zod branded PaymentIntent and Refund IDs and statuses, the TEST or LIVE environment type and timestamp helpers (event.created, or canceled_at for a canceled PaymentIntent).
nodes.detail: IDs are parsed with Zod and branded so a refund ID cannot be passed as a PaymentIntent ID. Status schemas list every Stripe status, which lets the mapping functions use exhaustive switches.

nodes.name: Payment method strategies
nodes.summary: One class per supported Stripe payment method: its Zod input schema, the flow it really supports and the payment_method_options to send.
nodes.detail: Each class implements PaymentMethod: getResolvedTransactionFlow turns Saleor's requested flow (CHARGE or AUTHORIZATION) into the one the method supports, and getCreatePaymentIntentMethodOptions returns the options block. Card keeps the requested flow and sets capture_method manual for authorization; SEPA Debit, for example, always charges because funds are not guaranteed until the debit clears.

nodes.name: CardPaymentMethod
nodes.summary: Supports both flows; sets card.capture_method to manual for authorization so storefronts need no flow-specific logic.

nodes.name: Other payment methods
nodes.summary: Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna, Link, MobilePay, Pay by Bank, PayPal, Revolut Pay, SEPA Debit and US bank account classes.
nodes.detail: SEPA Debit, Pay by Bank and US bank account return CHARGE from getResolvedTransactionFlow whatever Saleor asked; Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna, Link, MobilePay, PayPal and Revolut Pay keep the requested flow. Each adds its own payment_method_options entry.

nodes.name: mapPaymentIntentStatusToTransactionResult()
nodes.summary: Maps a PaymentIntent status plus the recorded flow to a Saleor result: succeeded is CHARGE_SUCCESS, requires_capture AUTHORIZATION_SUCCESS, processing a REQUEST, the rest ACTION_REQUIRED.
nodes.detail: requires_payment_method, requires_confirmation, requires_action and canceled all become CHARGE_ or AUTHORIZATION_ACTION_REQUIRED with a status-specific message. assertUnreachable makes a new Stripe status a compile error.

nodes.name: mapRefundStatusToTransactionResult()
nodes.summary: Maps refund statuses: succeeded is REFUND_SUCCESS, pending and requires_action REFUND_REQUEST, failed and canceled REFUND_FAILURE.

nodes.name: Result classes
nodes.summary: ActionRequired, Success, Failure, Request, Cancel and Refund result classes, each with the Saleor result, allowed actions and message.
nodes.detail: ActionRequired results build their message from the Stripe status and throw for statuses they do not support. CHARGE_FAILURE allows CHARGE and AUTHORIZATION_FAILURE allows CANCEL; refund results carry REFUND_SUCCESS, REFUND_FAILURE or REFUND_REQUEST.

nodes.name: TransactionEventReporter
nodes.summary: Calls Saleor's transactionEventReport mutation with the installation's app token and classifies the answer.

nodes.name: reportTransactionEvent()
nodes.summary: Sends transactionEventReport, using the variant with paymentMethodDetails when card details are known; maps ALREADY_EXISTS and alreadyProcessed to AlreadyReportedError.
nodes.detail: Network or server errors become ServerError, GRAPHQL_ERROR a GraphqlError, INVALID, NOT_FOUND, INCORRECT_DETAILS and REQUIRED an UnhandledError. When several mutation errors come back only the first is handled and the rest are logged. The use case treats AlreadyReportedError as success, which makes Stripe's retries idempotent.

const mutationResult = await this.gqlClient.mutation(

          type: input.type,

          paymentMethodDetails: input.saleorPaymentMethodDetailsInput,

nodes.name: SaleorMoney
nodes.summary: Converts Stripe integer amounts back to Saleor decimals with the currency's digit count.

nodes.name: SaleorPaymentMethodDetails
nodes.summary: Maps a Stripe payment method to Saleor's payment method details: card name, brand, last digits and expiry for cards, the type name otherwise.

nodes.name: Requested-event payload helpers
nodes.summary: Reads the transaction, channel ID and idempotency key from charge, refund and cancel requested payloads whether the source is an order or a checkout.
nodes.detail: The channel comes from transaction.checkout.channel or transaction.order.channel because the GraphQL schema makes both optional. The idempotency key exists on payloads from Saleor 3.23; without it the Stripe SDK generates its own key, which only covers retries within one request.

nodes.name: ChannelsFetcher
nodes.summary: Runs the FetchChannels GraphQL query for the channel assignment screen.

nodes.name: Saleor value types
nodes.summary: Branded SaleorApiUrl (an address ending in /graphql/), Saleor and resolved transaction flows (CHARGE or AUTHORIZATION) and the transaction ID.
nodes.detail: createSaleorApiUrl returns a Result and requires an address ending in /graphql/. Flow types accept only AUTHORIZATION or CHARGE; the resolved flow can differ from the requested one when the payment method cannot authorize.

nodes.name: StripeConfig
nodes.summary: Validated configuration: name, IDs, keys and webhook secret; rejects keys from different environments and derives TEST or LIVE from the publishable key prefix.
nodes.detail: StripeFrontendConfig is the safe copy sent to the browser: keys are masked to their last four characters. AppRootConfig (app-root-config.ts) holds all configurations by ID plus the channel to configuration map.

nodes.name: AppConfigRepo interface
nodes.summary: Storage contract: save, get by channel ID or configuration ID, get the root config, remove a configuration and update a channel mapping.
nodes.detail: Two access patterns: by channel ID (Saleor webhooks know the channel) and by configuration ID (the Stripe webhook address carries it). The comments above the two access pattern types in the file describe them the other way round.

nodes.name: DynamodbAppConfigRepo
nodes.summary: dynamodb-toolbox implementation of AppConfigRepo; encrypts the restricted key and webhook secret with a RotatingEncryptor before writing.
nodes.detail: getStripeConfig by channel first reads the mapping item (SK CHANNEL_ID#...) to find the configuration ID, then the configuration item (SK CONFIG_ID#...). getRootConfig runs two queries in parallel over the installation's partition. Decryption tries SECRET_KEY first and then the fallback keys; a value no key can decrypt raises DecryptionError. Parsing failures are thrown inside and returned as FailureFetchingConfig.

nodes.name: DynamodbAppConfigRepo.getStripeConfig()
nodes.summary: Resolves a configuration by configuration ID, or by channel ID through the mapping item; returns null when either is missing.

nodes.name: DynamodbAppConfigRepo.saveStripeConfig()
nodes.summary: Writes the configuration item with the restricted key and webhook secret encrypted; the publishable key stays in clear text.

nodes.name: DynamoDB item models
nodes.summary: StripeConfig item (configName, configId, stripePk, stripeRk, stripeWhSecret, stripeWhId) and channel mapping item (channelId, optional configId), both under PK '<saleorApiUrl>#<appId>'.

nodes.name: appConfig tRPC router
nodes.summary: Binds the seven configuration procedures and shares one StripeWebhookManager between them.
nodes.detail: Each procedure is a class with getTrpcProcedure() so dependencies such as the webhook manager or channel fetcher can be injected in tests.

nodes.name: saveNewStripeConfig procedure
nodes.summary: Validates keys, checks the restricted key against Stripe, creates the Stripe webhook endpoint and saves the encrypted configuration.
nodes.detail: Generates a configuration ID, validates the model with placeholder webhook values, calls StripeAuthValidator, then StripeWebhookManager.createWebhook with the app address taken from the request's Origin header. The returned signing secret is validated and the final StripeConfig saved through ctx.configRepo. Errors become tRPC errors (BAD_REQUEST, UNAUTHORIZED, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR).

nodes.name: updateStripeConfig procedure
nodes.summary: Renames a configuration or rotates its keys; recreates the Stripe endpoint when the new key cannot see the old one.
nodes.detail: An empty restricted key keeps the stored one. Publishable and restricted keys must belong to the same environment. When keys change it validates the key, asks isWebhookReachableWithKey, and if the endpoint is not visible creates a new one on the new account and deletes the old one with the old key before saving. A rename updates the endpoint description after the response.

nodes.name: removeStripeConfig procedure
nodes.summary: Deletes the configuration's Stripe endpoint, clears channel mappings that pointed to it and removes the item.

nodes.name: getStripeConfigsList procedure
nodes.summary: Lists configurations as masked StripeFrontendConfig objects with each endpoint's live status (active, disabled or missing) read from Stripe.

nodes.name: Channel mapping procedures
nodes.summary: updateMapping assigns or clears a channel's configuration; channelsConfigsMapping and fetchChannels feed the assignment screen.

nodes.name: protectedClientProcedure
nodes.summary: tRPC middleware chain: loads auth data from the APL (Auth Persistence Layer), verifies the dashboard user's JSON Web Token (JWT) and attaches a GraphQL client.
nodes.detail: attachAppToken reads saleorApiUrl from the request header and the app token from the APL (401 when missing). validateClientToken calls verifyJWT from the app SDK with the app ID and any required permissions. attachSharedServices creates the GraphQL client with the user's token, not the app token.

nodes.name: Root tRPC router
nodes.summary: Combines appConfig and orderSync routers; throws if imported in the browser so server-only modules never reach the bundle.
nodes.detail: trpc-server.ts sets REQUIRED_CLIENT_PERMISSIONS as default procedure metadata and context-app-router.ts reads the token, Saleor address and Origin headers. The router file throws when evaluated in a browser because it imports DynamoDB and the AWS SDK.

nodes.name: trpcClient
nodes.summary: React Query tRPC client the pages use; its batch link (@saleor/apps-trpc) adds the Saleor API address and dashboard token headers from App Bridge.
nodes.detail: createTRPCNext with ssr false and refetching on mount, focus and reconnect disabled; the pages read and mutate configuration through it.

nodes.name: Order sync enablement
nodes.summary: Lets staff on older installations grant MANAGE_ORDERS and then registers the ORDER_CREATED webhook from the app.
nodes.detail: ORDER_CREATED needs MANAGE_ORDERS. New installations get both from the manifest; older ones see a callout, staff grant the permission in the dashboard and the app then creates the webhook itself through webhookCreate. The deploy migration keeps the webhook only where it exists.

nodes.name: OrderSyncInstaller
nodes.summary: Reads the app's permissions and webhooks with the app token, and creates the ORDER_CREATED webhook once MANAGE_ORDERS is granted.
nodes.detail: Only the enabled state is cached, in memory per serverless instance for one hour; a missing permission is always checked again because staff can grant it at any moment.

nodes.name: orderSync tRPC router
nodes.summary: getStatus and enable procedures; builds a GraphQL client with the app token because the staff token cannot see the app's own data.
nodes.detail: Extends protectedClientProcedure with a client using the app token and a cache key '<saleorApiUrl>:<appId>'. enable builds the webhook manifest from APP_API_BASE_URL or the request Origin and maps a missing permission to PRECONDITION_FAILED.

nodes.name: RecordedTransaction
nodes.summary: PaymentIntent ID, Saleor transaction ID, requested and resolved flow, selected payment method and Saleor schema version.

nodes.name: TransactionRecorderRepo interface
nodes.summary: recordTransaction and getTransactionByStripePaymentIntentId, with TransactionMissingError when nothing was recorded.
nodes.detail: transaction-recorder-impl.ts exports the single DynamoDB instance; a fork can replace that one file to use another store.

nodes.name: DynamoDBTransactionRecorderRepo
nodes.summary: Puts the record with condition paymentIntentId does not exist (an existing item counts as success) and gets it by PK and SK TRANSACTION#<paymentIntentId>.

nodes.name: Environment schema
nodes.summary: @t3-oss/env-nextjs schema for every environment variable: SECRET_KEY, APL, DynamoDB table and timeouts, AWS (Amazon Web Services) region and role, OpenTelemetry, Sentry, cron and cleanup settings.
nodes.detail: Server variables are validated at start-up and errors formatted by @saleor/errors. Secret key rotation and stale cleanup variables are merged in from shared schemas (newSecretKeyServerSchema, staleInstallationsCleanupServerSchema).
facts: APL defaults to file; dynamodb in production

nodes.name: SaleorApp and APL
nodes.summary: Chooses the APL (Auth Persistence Layer): DynamoAPL on the main DynamoDB table when APL=dynamodb, otherwise a local FileAPL.
nodes.detail: The APL maps a Saleor API address to the app ID and token. FileAPL writes a local file and is meant for development only; DynamoAPL shares the main table with configuration data using a PK without the app ID.

nodes.name: AppContextContainer
nodes.summary: AsyncLocalStorage holding the request's Stripe environment (TEST or LIVE) so responses can show detailed errors only for test configurations.
nodes.detail: wrapRequest starts a fresh context per request; set() also copies the value into the logger context. Reading outside a request returns the default (stripeEnv null) with a warning.

nodes.name: App logger setup
nodes.summary: Configures the shared tslog root logger: console transport in development, Sentry and Vercel runtime transports in production, and replaces the masked key list with token and secretKey.
nodes.detail: The production transports are imported lazily on the server only. The assignment to rootLogger.settings.maskValuesOfKeys replaces the shared package's longer default list (which includes restrictedKey, webhookSecret and clientSecret) with just token and secretKey.

nodes.name: Instrumented GraphQL client
nodes.summary: createInstrumentedGraphqlClient: urql client for a Saleor instance with the app's user agent and an OpenTelemetry exchange that records one span per operation.

nodes.name: BaseError and small utilities
nodes.summary: modern-errors BaseError with an _internalName prop and serialization, plus assertUnreachable and RandomId (UUID, universally unique identifier, generator).
nodes.detail: Every app error is a BaseError subclass with an _internalName prop, so errors are typed nominally and serialize without stacks into logs and Sentry.

nodes.name: Observability attribute setters
nodes.summary: Copy the Saleor API address, Saleor version and source object ID into the logger context and Sentry tags.

nodes.name: Required dashboard permissions
nodes.summary: MANAGE_APPS and HANDLE_PAYMENTS: the permissions a dashboard user needs; default meta of every tRPC procedure and the UI access check.

nodes.name: Next.js instrumentation
nodes.summary: Loads OpenTelemetry when OTEL_ENABLED is true and Sentry when NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN is set; forwards request errors to Sentry.
nodes.detail: otel-node registers @vercel/otel with a batch span processor (OTLP, OpenTelemetry Protocol, over HTTP with an optional x-alb-access-token header) and AWS and HTTP instrumentations, while Sentry skips its own OpenTelemetry setup and keeps only error tracking. The browser side (instrumentation-client.ts) initializes Sentry and ignores TRPCClientError.

nodes.name: DynamoDB main table
nodes.summary: One dynamodb-toolbox table with string PK and SK holding APL entries, configurations, channel mappings and recorded transactions.
nodes.detail: Installation-scoped data uses PK '<saleorApiUrl>#<appId>' so a reinstall cannot see old data; the APL uses PK '<saleorApiUrl>' so it survives reinstalls. The client uses Vercel OIDC (OpenID Connect) role credentials when AWS_ROLE_ARN is set, static keys otherwise, and explicit request and connection timeouts.

nodes.name: StripeProblemReporter
nodes.summary: Reports configuration problems as Saleor App Problems shown to staff: invalid key, missing permission, webhook secret mismatch, missing or orphaned config, unsupported method, foreign objects.
nodes.detail: Each problem has a stable key per configuration or channel and criticalThreshold 1. reportApiProblem only reports Stripe authentication and permission errors. clearProblemsForConfig dismisses a configuration's problems after it is updated or removed. Reporting runs in next/server after() so it never delays the webhook answer.

nodes.name: Pages
nodes.summary: Next.js Pages Router: _app (App Bridge, GraphQL and theme providers, iframe guard), the index redirect, and config list, new and edit pages.

nodes.name: Configuration form views
nodes.summary: Create and edit forms with key fields, environment badge, key prefix hints, unsaved-change guard and remove action.

nodes.name: Configuration list and cards
nodes.summary: Cards for each configuration with webhook status and assigned channels; delete and channel unassignment call tRPC mutations.

nodes.name: Channel assignment
nodes.summary: Assigns channels to configurations; build-channel-move-plan computes the mapping updates and a modal confirms moves between configurations.

nodes.name: Setup checklist card
nodes.summary: Dismissible guided-setup card summarizing which steps (keys, channels) are done, plus the TEST and LIVE legend.

nodes.name: Order sync callout
nodes.summary: Shows when MANAGE_ORDERS or the ORDER_CREATED webhook is missing and calls orderSync.enable.

nodes.name: Access check hook
nodes.summary: Checks the dashboard user has the required permissions; pages render MissingAppAccess otherwise.

nodes.name: Stripe app package
nodes.summary: saleor-app-payment-stripe package: Next.js scripts, codegen, migrate, rotate-secret-key, setup-dynamodb and unit, integration and end-to-end test commands.

nodes.name: Vercel settings
nodes.summary: Daily cleanup cron at 03:00 and deployment regions dub1 and iad1.

nodes.name: Environment example
nodes.summary: Lists the variables a local run needs (SECRET_KEY, DynamoDB endpoint and table, cron and cleanup settings) without values for secrets.

nodes.name: GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Subscription queries for the seven webhooks, the transactionEventReport mutations, FetchChannels and FetchOrderSyncStatus queries, and shared fragments.
nodes.detail: Each subscription includes the EventMetadata fragment (Saleor version and recipient app ID) used for the recipient check. Codegen (graphql.config.ts) turns them into typed documents in generated/graphql.ts.

nodes.name: Generated types
nodes.summary: generated/graphql.ts from codegen and app-webhooks-types: response types compiled from Saleor's JSON schemas for each synchronous webhook.

nodes.name: Webhooks migration script
nodes.summary: Run on every deploy: for each installation in the APL, rewrites the app's Saleor webhooks to match the current definitions.
nodes.detail: Computes the base address from each installation's appUrl, keeps the enabled state (all on if any is on) and adds ORDER_CREATED only where it already exists, because the runner deletes every webhook missing from the list and older installations lack MANAGE_ORDERS. Errors per installation go to Sentry; --dry-run only logs.

nodes.name: Deploy script
nodes.summary: Sets SENTRY_RELEASE from the package version, runs next build and then the webhooks migration.

nodes.name: Secret key rotation script
nodes.summary: Re-encrypts stripeRk and stripeWhSecret in DynamoDB from the old keys to the new SECRET_KEY; exits 1 when any item fails.

nodes.name: Local DynamoDB setup
nodes.summary: Creates the main table (PK and SK strings) on a local DynamoDB endpoint, default http://localhost:8000.

nodes.name: Webhook response type generator
nodes.summary: Downloads Saleor's JSON schemas for the six synchronous payment webhooks from the Saleor GitHub repository and compiles them to TypeScript.

nodes.name: Test runner configs
nodes.summary: Vitest projects (unit, integration) and Playwright end-to-end settings; integration tests use local DynamoDB and the real Stripe test API.

nodes.name: Stripe app README
nodes.summary: Local setup (Node 24+, pnpm 10+, dev containers, port 3000), tunnels for Saleor Cloud, integration and end-to-end test instructions.

nodes.name: Monorepo root and decisions
nodes.summary: Root README and agent guides, pnpm and Turborepo configuration and the architecture decision records.
nodes.detail: Turborepo runs build, lint, type checks and tests across apps and packages; packages are linked with workspace:* dependencies. ADRs (architecture decision records) document cross-app choices such as branded types and the dashboard-aligned UI kit.

nodes.name: Contributor and agent guide
nodes.summary: Monorepo conventions: neverthrow Result handling, Zod branded types, BaseError subclasses, repository pattern on DynamoDB, use case classes per webhook.

nodes.name: Architecture decision records
nodes.summary: ADR (architecture decision record) 0001 record decisions, 0002 Zod branded types, 0003 Socket.dev dependency checks, 0004 dashboard-aligned UI package.

nodes.name: Workspace configuration
nodes.summary: Root pnpm workspace scripts and the Turborepo task graph (build, check-types, lint, test, generate).

nodes.name: @saleor/webhook-utils
nodes.summary: Creates, modifies and removes an app's Saleor webhooks from manifests, used by deploy-time migrations and order sync.
nodes.detail: Webhooks are matched by name: manifests with no existing webhook are created, matches are updated, existing ones missing from the manifest list are removed. Errors are classified into permission denied (app probably uninstalled), network and unknown so a migration over many installations can continue.

nodes.name: WebhookMigrationRunner
nodes.summary: Fetches app details and Saleor version, asks the app for its target manifests and hands the diff to WebhookUpdater; permission and network errors become warnings.

nodes.name: WebhookUpdater
nodes.summary: Matches existing webhooks to manifests by name, then adds, updates and removes; on any error tries to roll back the changes made so far.

nodes.name: Webhook GraphQL operations
nodes.summary: createAppWebhook, modifyAppWebhook, removeAppWebhook and the app details and Saleor instance queries, each mapping PermissionDenied and network errors to typed errors.
nodes.detail: Each operation runs one GraphQL document through urql and throws WebhookMigrationAppPermissionDeniedError on PermissionDenied, WebhookMigrationNetworkError on network errors and WebhookMigrationUnknownError when the mutation returns no webhook.

nodes.name: APP_DELETED handler factory
nodes.summary: Builds an asynchronous APP_DELETED webhook that deletes the APL entry and runs optional hooks; the Stripe app does not subscribe to it.

nodes.name: @saleor/dynamo-config-repository
nodes.summary: Generic DynamoDB repository for channel-mapped app configurations; the Stripe app has its own copy of the pattern and does not import it.
nodes.detail: Mapping items (channelId, optional configId) and config items share a table; the app supplies converters between its domain config and the DynamoDB item. In this checkout only another app's package depends on it.

nodes.name: DynamoConfigRepository
nodes.summary: Generic config repo over a dynamodb-toolbox table: config items plus channel mapping items, with mapping functions supplied by each app.

nodes.name: Repository test bootstrap
nodes.summary: Test helper that builds a table and entity for the repository tests.

nodes.name: @saleor/apps-logger
nodes.summary: tslog-based root logger with masking, request-scoped context and transports for console, Sentry and Vercel logs.
nodes.detail: Apps attach transports at start-up depending on environment. LoggerContext attributes (Saleor address, version, PSP reference, meaning payment service provider reference) are added to each line by the Vercel transport.

nodes.name: rootLogger
nodes.summary: tslog Logger whose level comes from APP_LOG_LEVEL (default info) and which masks secret-like keys (password, secret, webhookSecret, restrictedKey, token...) case-insensitively.
nodes.detail: Masking applies to log call arguments at any depth for every transport; attributes passed to getSubLogger are not masked. Apps can overwrite settings.maskValuesOfKeys, which replaces this list.

nodes.name: LoggerContext
nodes.summary: AsyncLocalStorage of attributes added to every log line; wrapWithLoggerContextAppRouter opens one per request.

nodes.name: Sentry transport
nodes.summary: Turns error-level logs that carry an Error into Sentry exceptions and records log lines as Sentry breadcrumbs.

nodes.name: Vercel runtime transport
nodes.summary: Prints structured JSON log lines with version and logger context for Vercel log drains.

nodes.name: @saleor/errors
nodes.summary: Shared BaseError (modern-errors with serialization, stack excluded) and formatEnvValidationError for readable environment errors.
nodes.detail: BaseError adds a _brand prop for nominal typing; formatEnvValidationError prints each failing environment variable with its message.

nodes.name: @saleor/apps-otel
nodes.summary: OpenTelemetry helpers: span processor and metrics exporter factories, instrumentations, the urql exchange and span attribute wrappers.
nodes.detail: Apps register @vercel/otel with these factories; the urql exchange and span attribute wrappers attach Saleor-specific attributes (API address, version) so traces can be filtered per store.

nodes.name: Span and metrics exporters
nodes.summary: BatchSpanProcessor and metrics reader using OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) over HTTP, sending the optional access token as x-alb-access-token.

nodes.name: urql OpenTelemetry exchange
nodes.summary: Starts a client span per GraphQL operation with its name, type, body and Saleor address, and ends it with the result status.

nodes.name: Span attribute wrappers
nodes.summary: Copies the Saleor API address and schema version headers onto the active span and sets the Sentry user.

nodes.name: @saleor/sentry-utils
nodes.summary: setSentrySaleorUser (Sentry user ID is the Saleor host) and exportSentryReleaseEnvironmentVariable for deploys.
nodes.detail: setSentrySaleorUser parses the Saleor address and uses only its host as the Sentry user ID, ignoring invalid addresses. The release helper sets SENTRY_RELEASE to the package version in production, or version plus commit hash elsewhere.

nodes.name: @saleor/stale-installations-cleanup
nodes.summary: Shared body of every app's cron that removes data of Saleor Cloud environments that no longer exist.
nodes.detail: Saleor Cloud is asked, with a short-lived Vercel OIDC (OpenID Connect) token, which installation hosts still exist. Only hosts under the configured root domains are judged; others are skipped. The app hook runs first, then the tenant's DynamoDB items are deleted in batches of 25.

nodes.name: cleanupStaleInstallations()
nodes.summary: Finds stale installations, runs the app's own deleteAppData hook, then deletes the tenant's DynamoDB items; refuses to delete when every checked installation looks stale.
nodes.detail: Returns HTTP-style status and body for the route: 201 Not configured when variables are missing, 502 when Saleor Cloud cannot be asked, 500 when every checked installation would be deleted (a sign SALEOR_CLOUD_API_URL is wrong), 200 with counts otherwise. Logs in chunks of 100 because Vercel keeps 256 lines per request. An installation whose hook throws is kept for the next run.

nodes.name: findStaleInstallations()
nodes.summary: Asks the Saleor Cloud API, with a Vercel OIDC (OpenID Connect) token for the configured audience, which installation hosts under the root domains still exist.

nodes.name: Tenant key scan and delete
nodes.summary: Scans the table for items whose PK belongs to a stale Saleor address and deletes them in batches.

nodes.name: @saleor/apps-shared
nodes.summary: Cross-app helpers: encryption and key rotation, cron auth, GraphQL client, metadata manager, compose, env schemas and React wrappers.
nodes.detail: Mostly small, dependency-light helpers imported by path (for example @saleor/apps-shared/encryptor). Key rotation reads SECRET_KEY plus fallback variables through secret-key-resolution.ts so apps can rotate keys without downtime.

nodes.name: Encryptor
nodes.summary: AES-256-CBC (Advanced Encryption Standard) with a random 16-byte IV (initialization vector) per value, stored as '<iv hex>:<ciphertext hex>'.

nodes.name: RotatingEncryptor
nodes.summary: Encrypts with the primary key and decrypts with the primary or any fallback key, warning when a fallback was needed; throws DecryptionError when none works.

nodes.name: Secret key rotation runner
nodes.summary: Re-encrypts named fields of every item from the old keys to the new key, with dry run and concurrent-modification detection; DynamoDB and metadata variants.

nodes.name: Cron auth guard
nodes.summary: withCronAuth and withCronAuthAppRouter: constant-time check of 'Bearer CRON_SECRET', refusing every request while the secret is unset.

nodes.name: createGraphQLClient()
nodes.summary: urql client that sends the token in Saleor's Authorization-Bearer header, a server-side User-Agent and optional extra exchanges.

nodes.name: Encrypted metadata manager
nodes.summary: Stores app settings as encrypted Saleor app metadata (used by apps without DynamoDB); not used by the Stripe app.

nodes.name: Small server helpers
nodes.summary: compose for route wrappers, REQUIRED_SALEOR_PERMISSIONS (MANAGE_APPS), race, app base address and Saleor version check.

nodes.name: React app wrappers
nodes.summary: GraphQLProvider, iframe guard, no-SSR (server-side rendering) wrapper, theme synchronizer and dashboard notification and unsaved-changes hooks.

nodes.name: @saleor/app-problems
nodes.summary: AppProblemsReporter: appProblemCreate and appProblemDismiss (by key) mutations so apps can surface problems to staff in the dashboard.

nodes.name: @saleor/app-deprecation
nodes.summary: Cron handler that sets deprecationReason on every installation with appSelfUpdate, in parallel workers with a per-installation timeout.

nodes.name: @saleor/apps-domain
nodes.summary: Shared branded SaleorApiUrl type used by the generic DynamoDB repository.
nodes.detail: Zod schema for an address ending in /graphql/, branded SaleorApiUrl, as recommended by ADR (architecture decision record) 0002.

nodes.name: @saleor/apps-trpc
nodes.summary: tRPC batch link that adds App Bridge's token and Saleor address headers, and a Pages Router context factory.
nodes.detail: http-batch-link.ts reads the token and Saleor address from App Bridge state and sends them as Saleor headers; context-pages-router.ts builds the context for apps still on the Pages Router API.

nodes.name: @saleor/apps-ui-next
nodes.summary: Dashboard-aligned component kit (detail layouts, settings cards, setup checklist, modals, chips) copied from Saleor Dashboard sources, per ADR (architecture decision record) 0004.

nodes.name: @saleor/apps-ui
nodes.summary: Older layout kit (Layout.AppSection, ConfigsList, EmptyConfigs, breadcrumbs) still used by most other apps.

nodes.name: @saleor/react-hook-form-macaw
nodes.summary: Macaw UI inputs bound to react-hook-form controllers.

flows.name: A shopper pays with Stripe
flows.summary: Saleor asks the Stripe app for a publishable key and a PaymentIntent, the shopper confirms with Stripe, and Stripe's event becomes a Saleor transaction event.

steps.text: The storefront calls paymentGatewayInitialize for the checkout's channel.
Saleor's mutation sends the synchronous PAYMENT_GATEWAY_INITIALIZE_SESSION webhook to every payment app.
The app verifies Saleor's signature and the recipient app ID.
It looks up the Stripe configuration mapped to the channel in DynamoDB and returns the publishable key for Stripe.js.
The storefront calls transactionInitialize with data.paymentIntent.paymentMethod, for example card; Saleor sends TRANSACTION_INITIALIZE_SESSION.
The use case parses the payment method, loads the configuration, decides the flow (charge or authorization) and builds the PaymentIntent with Saleor's idempotency key and metadata.
Stripe creates the PaymentIntent with the configuration's restricted key.
The app records which Saleor transaction and flow the PaymentIntent belongs to, then answers ACTION_REQUIRED with the client secret.
The storefront confirms the payment with Stripe.js using the client secret (outside this app).
Stripe sends payment_intent.succeeded (or amount_capturable_updated for authorizations) to the endpoint created for this configuration.
The app loads the installation and configuration, verifies the Stripe signature and checks the object's metadata belongs to this installation.
The handler reads the recorded flow and maps the status: succeeded becomes CHARGE_SUCCESS, requires_capture AUTHORIZATION_SUCCESS.
The app calls transactionEventReport with the amount, pspReference, time and card details.
Saleor records the event on the transaction, which can complete the checkout or mark the order paid.

flows.name: A refund requested in Saleor reaches Stripe
flows.summary: Staff refund a payment; the app creates a Stripe refund, answers asynchronously and later reports the refund's final status.

steps.text: Staff refund an order payment in the dashboard.
Saleor's transactionRequestAction mutation turns the refund request into a webhook for the app that owns the transaction.
Saleor sends the synchronous TRANSACTION_REFUND_REQUESTED webhook.
The route verifies the signature and recipient, then runs the use case.
The use case loads the channel's configuration, converts the amount to Stripe minor units and calls refunds.create with Saleor's idempotency key and transaction metadata.
Stripe creates the refund; the app answers only { pspReference: refund ID } because Saleor does not accept REFUND_REQUEST as a synchronous result.
When the refund settles Stripe sends charge.refund.updated.
The refund handler finds the PaymentIntent behind the refund, reads the recorded transaction and maps succeeded to REFUND_SUCCESS, failed or canceled to REFUND_FAILURE.
transactionEventReport records the refund result on the Saleor transaction.

flows.name: Staff connect a Stripe account
flows.summary: Staff save Stripe keys in the app screen; the app checks them, creates a Stripe webhook endpoint and stores the encrypted configuration.

steps.text: Staff open the Stripe app inside the dashboard and fill in a name, publishable key and restricted key.
The page calls saveNewStripeConfig with the dashboard token and Saleor address headers.
The middleware loads the app's auth data and verifies the user's token and permissions.
The handler validates both keys belong to the same environment and tests the restricted key against Stripe.
It registers /api/webhooks/stripe with the configuration ID, Saleor address and app ID in the query, subscribed to seven events.
The configuration is saved with the restricted key and signing secret encrypted by SECRET_KEY.
Staff then assign channels; each channel maps to one configuration.
